title: Small talk and likes
goal: Chat about the weather, how you feel, what you're doing right now and what you like.

notes.p: {{鍾意|zung1 ji3}} means 'to like'. Put the thing or activity straight after it. To ask, split it: {{鍾唔鍾意|zung1 m4 zung1 ji3}} (only the first syllable repeats). Answer by repeating the verb: {{鍾意|zung1 ji3}} or {{唔鍾意|m4 zung1 ji3}}.
ex: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 tai2 hei3 aa3

notes.p: {{緊|gan2}} goes right after the verb for something going on right now, like English '-ing'. If the verb has an object, {{緊|gan2}} sits between them: {{食緊飯|sik6 gan2 faan6}}, {{瞓緊覺|fan3 gan2 gaau3}}. It never goes before the verb or at the end of the sentence.

{{好|hou2}} before an adjective means 'very' (often just 'is'): {{好凍|hou2 dung3}} = it's cold. {{幾|gei2}} before an adjective means 'pretty, fairly': {{幾凍|gei2 dung3}}. For weather there is no word for 'it': just say the adjective. {{都|dou1}} = 'also, too'. It goes after the person and before the verb: {{我都鍾意|ngo5 dou1 zung1 ji3}}, never at the end like English 'too'.

notes.h: Is that right? Are you free?
notes.p: {{係咪|hai6 mai6}} is {{係唔係|hai6 m4 hai6}} squeezed together. Put it before what you're checking: {{你係咪好攰呀？|nei5 hai6 mai6 hou2 gui6 aa3}} 'Are you tired?' On its own, {{係咪呀？|hai6 mai6 aa3}} = 'Is that right?' {{得閒|dak1 haan4}} = free (not busy). Ask with {{得唔得閒|dak1 m4 dak1 haan4}} and answer {{得閒|dak1 haan4}} or {{唔得閒|m4 dak1 haan4}}.
ex: 你今個週末得唔得閒呀？
nei5 gam1 go3 zau1 mut6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3
ni1 go3 hai6 mai6 nei5 ge3 aa3

notes.p: {{呀|aa3}} softens a question or remark so it doesn't sound blunt. {{啦|laa1}} makes a suggestion or a friendly push: 'let's', 'go ahead'. {{喇|laa3}} marks a change: something is now so. {{㗎|gaa3}} adds 'you know', explaining or insisting. Sound tip: {{啦|laa1}} is high and level, {{喇|laa3}} sits in the middle, so listen for the pitch.
ex: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 haang4 gaai1 laa1
ni1 go3 hou2 hou2 sik6 gaa3
This is really tasty, you know.

vocab.note: 緊 (gan2) after a verb = "-ing, right now".

t: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 jam2 caa4 aa3
vocab.note: With a two-syllable verb only the first syllable repeats: 鍾唔鍾意.

t: nei5 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3
vocab.en: Are you free? (Do you have time?)

vocab.note: 係咪 is 係唔係 ("is or isn't") squeezed together.
The second 慢 rises to maan2. A host says this to a departing guest.

t: ni1 go3 hai6 mat1 je5 lai4 gaa3

vocab.note: {{都|dou1}} = also. It goes before the verb, never at the end.
Ask with {{得唔得閒|dak1 m4 dak1 haan4}}.
Literally 'fall rain'. Careful: {{雨|jyu5}} rain is low rising; {{魚|jyu2}} fish is high rising.

vocab.en: to go out shopping / stroll around
vocab.note: Wandering round the shops, not necessarily buying.
Used for both 'it's boring' and 'I'm bored'.

items.why: {{緊|gan2}} right after the verb means it's happening now: {{落緊雨|lok6 gan2 jyu5}}.
{{咩|me1}} = what. {{邊度|bin1 dou6}} is where, {{邊個|bin1 go3}} is who.
{{攰|gui6}} = tired. {{貴|gwai3}} sounds a bit similar but means expensive; {{忙|mong4}} is busy, {{飽|baau2}} is full.
{{凍|dung3}} (mid level tone) = cold. {{東|dung1}} is high and means east; {{熱|jit6}} is hot; {{痛|tung3}} is painful.
{{聽歌|teng1 go1}} = listen to songs. {{睇戲|tai2 hei3}} is watching movies, {{行街|haang4 gaai1}} is going shopping, {{瞓覺|fan3 gaau3}} is sleeping.
{{呢|ne1}} after a person asks 'and you?': {{你呢？|nei5 ne1}}.
{{緊|gan2}} goes right after the verb, before the object: {{食緊飯|sik6 gan2 faan6}}.
{{等緊|dang2 gan2}} = waiting right now. {{等陣|dang2 zan6}} means 'wait a moment' and can't take 'you' after it.
{{幾|gei2}} before an adjective = pretty, fairly. {{太|taai3}} is 'too', {{唔|m4}} is 'not'.
{{都|dou1}} = also, and it goes before the verb. {{我好鍾意|ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3}} would be 'I really like it'.
A-not-A question with {{唔|m4}}: {{得唔得閒|dak1 m4 dak1 haan4}}.

items.en: What time do you get off work?
items.why: {{收工|sau1 gung1}} = finish work. {{返工|faan1 gung1}} is going to work.
{{係咪|hai6 mai6}} (= {{係唔係|hai6 m4 hai6}}) asks 'is it…?'. {{係唔|hai6 m4}} is only half of {{係唔係|hai6 m4 hai6}}.

q: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 tai2 hei3 ___
items.en: Let's go see a movie together.
items.why: {{啦|laa1}} turns the sentence into a suggestion, 'let's'. {{咩|me1}} would make it a surprised question.

items.en: This is really tasty, you know.
items.why: {{㗎|gaa3}} adds 'you know', insisting. {{喇|laa3}} would mean it has now become tasty; {{咩|me1}} makes a doubtful question.
{{喇|laa3}} marks a change: you weren't hungry, now you are.

items.q: A friend you haven't seen for a year walks into the café. You say:
items.why: {{好耐冇見|hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3}} = long time no see. {{下次見|haa6 ci3 gin3}} is for saying goodbye.

items.q: It's eleven at night and you're going to bed. You say to your family:
items.why: {{早唞|zou2 tau2}} = good night. {{早晨|zou2 san4}} starts the same but means good morning.

items.q: Friends had dinner at your flat. As they leave, you, the host, say:
items.why: A host sees guests off with {{慢慢行|maan6 maan2 haang4}}. {{一直行|jat1 zik6 haang4}} is a direction: go straight.

items.q: Wing asks how the new dim sum place was. It was decent: fine, nothing special. You say:
items.why: {{唔錯|m4 co3}} = not bad. {{好正|hou2 zeng3}} is 'awesome', too strong here.

items.q: You want to ask a friend whether they like coffee. You say:
opts: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 jam2 gaa3 fe1 aa3
nei5 zung1 m4 ji3 jam2 gaa3 fe1 aa3
nei5 zung1 ji3 m4 jam2 gaa3 fe1 aa3
nei5 zung1 ji3 jam2 gaa3 fe1 laa1
items.why: Only the first syllable repeats: {{鍾唔鍾意|zung1 m4 zung1 ji3}}. {{啦|laa1}} is for suggestions, not questions.

items.q: Ka-yan texts you {{你做緊咩呀？|nei5 zou6 gan2 me1 aa3}} You're watching a movie at home. You reply:
items.why: {{緊|gan2}} goes straight after the verb {{睇|tai2}}, before the object: {{睇緊戲|tai2 gan2 hei3}}.

items.q: Ka-yan asks {{你係美國人，係咪呀？|nei5 hai6 mei5 gwok3 jan4, hai6 mai6 aa3}} It's true. You confirm:
items.why: {{啱|ngaam1}} = that's right. {{係咪呀？|hai6 mai6 aa3}} would just ask her back.

items.q: It's a sweltering July day. You comment on the heat to your neighbour:
opts: gam1 jat6 jit6 m4 jit6 aa3
items.why: {{好熱|hou2 jit6}} = really hot. {{熱唔熱|jit6 m4 jit6}} would be asking, not commenting.

full: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 tai2 hei3 aa3
nei5 ting1 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3

items.en: I'm tired; I want to go home.
full: ngo5 hou2 gui6, soeng2 faan1 uk1 kei2
nei5 hai6 mai6 hou2 mong4 aa3
ngo5 lou5 po4 fan3 gan2 gaau3
ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 haang4 gaai1 laa1

items.en: This one is really pretty, you know.

items.why: {{緊|gan2}} = happening now. No {{唔|m4}}, no question particle.

opts: It's going to be cold tomorrow.
items.why: {{今日|gam1 jat6}} today, {{凍|dung3}} cold. Tomorrow would be {{聽日|ting1 jat6}}.
{{攰|gui6}} tired is low level; {{貴|gwai3}} expensive is mid level with a 'w'.

opts: What do you do for work?
items.why: {{做緊|zou6 gan2}} = doing right now. Work would be {{做咩工|zou6 me1 gung1}}.

say: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 teng1 go1 aa3
opts: Do you like listening to music?
Does she like listening to music?
items.why: {{鍾唔鍾意|zung1 m4 zung1 ji3}} asks 'do you like'; {{聽歌|teng1 go1}} is listening to music.

opts: I don't really like it either.
items.why: {{我|ngo5}} I, {{都|dou1}} too, {{好鍾意|hou2 zung1 ji3}} really like. We would be {{我哋|ngo5 dei6}}.

say: nei5 ting1 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3
items.why: {{聽日|ting1 jat6}} tomorrow; {{得唔得閒|dak1 m4 dak1 haan4}} = free or not?
{{好耐|hou2 noi6}} a long time, {{冇見|mou5 gin3}} haven't seen.

opts: She's on her way to work.
items.why: {{返緊屋企|faan1 gan2 uk1 kei2}} = going home right now. At home would be {{喺屋企|hai2 uk1 kei2}}.
{{幾好|gei2 hou2}} = pretty good.

s: hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3! zeoi3 gan6 dim2 aa3
turns.en: Long time no see! How have you been?

turns.why: Answer and ask back with {{你呢？|nei5 ne1}}. The others are goodbyes.

s: ngo5 dou1 gei2 hou2. nei5 zou6 gan2 me1 aa3
turns.en: I'm pretty good too. What are you up to?

turns.why: {{緊|gan2}} goes right after the verb {{返|faan1}}: {{返緊屋企|faan1 gan2 uk1 kei2}}.
She's leaving, so say bye: {{拜拜|baai1 baai3}}.
Agree with {{係呀|hai6 aa3}} and repeat {{好熱|hou2 jit6}}. {{凍|dung3}} is cold.

s: nei5 dei6 zi1 gaa1 go1 jit6 m4 jit6 gaa3
turns.en: What about Chicago, where you're from? Is it hot there?

turns.why: Answer an A-not-A question by repeating the word: {{熱呀|jit6 aa3}}. {{唔熱|m4 jit6}} contradicts {{好熱|hou2 jit6}}.

s: 係咪呀？你鍾唔鍾意香港呀？
hai6 mai6 aa3? nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 hoeng1 gong2 aa3
turns.en: Is that right? Do you like Hong Kong?

turns.why: Say yes by repeating the verb: {{鍾意|zung1 ji3}}.

s: 你今個週末得唔得閒呀？
nei5 gam1 go3 zau1 mut6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3

turns.why: Answer by repeating the word: {{得閒|dak1 haan4}}. The other two just ask the question back.

s: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 tai2 hei3 laa1

hou2 aa3! ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 tai2 gan2 hei3
hou2 aa3! ngo5 hou2 tai2 hei3 zung1 ji3

Echo her: {{星期六見|sing1 kei4 luk6 gin3}}. {{早唞|zou2 tau2}} means good night.

roleplay.title: Small talk in the lift
roleplay.setup: You meet your Hong Kong neighbour in the lift on a hot morning. Chat about the weather, how you're feeling and what you like doing.
roleplay.persona: You are Auntie Wong, a friendly retired neighbour in her sixties in a Hong Kong housing block. It is a hot, humid summer morning and it may rain later. Comment on the weather, ask how the learner is, whether they're busy or tired, what they are doing today, and whether they like Hong Kong food and dim sum. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-5: 好 / 幾 + adjective, 緊 for actions happening now, 鍾唔鍾意, 係咪, and natural particles 呀 啦 喇 㗎. Keep sentences short and repeat or slow down if asked.
opening: zou2 san4! gam1 jat6 hou2 jit6 aa3, hai6 mai6
roleplay.opening_en: Morning! It's so hot today, isn't it?
goals: Agree or disagree about the weather
Say one thing you like doing

roleplay.title: Catching up with Wing
roleplay.setup: You run into Wing, a friend you haven't seen for a long time. Catch up and find something you'd both like to do this weekend.
roleplay.persona: You are Wing, a cheerful Hong Kong friend in your thirties. You haven't seen the learner for a long time. Ask how they've been, what they're doing these days, whether they're busy, and whether they're free this weekend. You like watching movies and going shopping, and you don't like hot weather. Suggest doing something together with 啦. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-5, with 緊, 鍾意, 得唔得閒, 都 and 幾. Short sentences.
opening: hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3! zeoi3 gan6 dim2 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: Long time no see! How have you been?
goals: Say whether you're free this weekend
Agree on something you both like
